## Data generation

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 1: Installation and loading the "bridge" to Python
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# First set the path to the appropriate Python
library(reticulate)

# Set path to Python with scikit-learn installed
use_python("C:/your/path/to/python.exe")

# Now try to import sklearn
tryCatch({
  # Import sklearn.datasets module from Python
  skds <- import("sklearn.datasets")
  cat("SUCCESS: sklearn imported successfully!\n")
}, error = function(e) {
  # Error handling: display helpful messages if import fails
  cat("ERROR: Cannot import 'sklearn'. \n")
  cat("Error message:", e$message, "\n")
  cat("Make sure Python and 'scikit-learn' package are installed on your system.\n")
  cat("Run in terminal: py -m pip install scikit-learn\n")
})

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 2: "Transferring" the function from Python to R
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# If import successful, continue
if (exists("skds")) {
  # Create an R function that is actually a Python object
  make_classification <- skds$make_classification
  
  cat("SUCCESS: make_classification function transferred to R!\n")
} else {
  cat("Cannot proceed - sklearn not available.\n")
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Step 3: Data generation
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Helper function to convert Python results to R data frame
convert_to_df <- function(py_data) {
  # Extract features (X) - in Python this is index 0, in R it's [[1]]
  X <- py_data[[1]]
  # Extract target labels (y) - in Python this is index 1, in R it's [[2]]
  y <- py_data[[2]]
  
  # Convert the feature matrix to R data frame
  df <- as.data.frame(X)
  # Change column names to V1, V2, ... V10 for better readability
  colnames(df) <- paste0("V", 1:ncol(df)) 
  # Add the target variable as a factor with descriptive class names
  df$Class <- y
  return(df)
}

# --- Scenario 1: Low predictive power ---
# n_features=10, n_informative=2, n_redundant=2, class_sep=0.5
py_data_low <- make_classification(
  n_samples = 1000L,      # Generate 1000 samples (L tells R to treat as integer)
  n_features = 10L,       # Total number of features
  n_informative = 2L,     # Only 2 features are actually predictive
  n_redundant = 2L,       # 2 features are redundant (correlated with informative ones)
  shuffle = FALSE,        # first: informative, then: redundant, then noninformative
  n_clusters_per_class = 1L, # Good practice to simplify the problem
  class_sep = 0.5,        # Small separation between classes (hard to distinguish)
  flip_y = 0.1,           # 10% label noise (randomly flipped labels)
  random_state = 123L     # Set seed for reproducibility
)
# Convert Python output to R data frame
data_low_power <- convert_to_df(py_data_low)
print("--- Scenario 1: Low predictive power (from Python) ---")
# Display class distribution
table(data_low_power$Class)


# --- Scenario 2: Medium predictive power ---
# n_features=10, n_informative=5, n_redundant=2, class_sep=1.0
py_data_med <- make_classification(
  n_samples = 1000L,      # 1000 samples
  n_features = 10L,       # 10 total features
  n_informative = 5L,     # 5 features are predictive (better than scenario 1)
  n_redundant = 2L,       # 2 redundant features
  shuffle = FALSE,        # first: informative, then: redundant, then noninformative
  n_clusters_per_class = 1L, # Single cluster per class
  class_sep = 1.0,        # Medium separation between classes
  flip_y = 0.05,          # Only 5% label noise (less than scenario 1)
  random_state = 123L     # Same seed for reproducibility
)
data_med_power <- convert_to_df(py_data_med)
print("--- Scenario 2: Medium predictive power (from Python) ---")
table(data_med_power$Class)


# --- Scenario 3: High predictive power ---
# n_features=10, n_informative=8, n_redundant=0, class_sep=2.0
py_data_high <- make_classification(
  n_samples = 1000L,      # 1000 samples
  n_features = 10L,       # 10 total features
  n_informative = 8L,     # 8 features are predictive (most features are useful)
  n_redundant = 0L,       # No redundant features
  shuffle = FALSE,        # first: informative, then: redundant, then noninformative
  n_clusters_per_class = 1L, # Single cluster per class
  class_sep = 2.0,        # Large separation between classes (easy to distinguish)
  flip_y = 0.0,           # No label noise (perfect labels)
  random_state = 123L     # Same seed for reproducibility
)
data_high_power <- convert_to_df(py_data_high)
print("--- Scenario 3: High predictive power (from Python) ---")
table(data_high_power$Class)


# --- Scenario 4: Imbalanced data ---
# Using medium power but with changed class balance (e.g., 90/10)
# This is done using the 'weights' argument
py_data_imb <- make_classification(
  n_samples = 1000L,      # 1000 samples
  n_features = 10L,       # 10 total features
  n_informative = 5L,     # 5 predictive features (same as medium power scenario)
  n_redundant = 2L,       # 2 redundant features
  shuffle = FALSE,        # first: informative, then: redundant, then noninformative
  n_clusters_per_class = 1L, # Single cluster per class
  class_sep = 1.0,        # Medium separation (same as scenario 2)
  weights = list(0.9, 0.1), # Class ratio 90% to 10% (highly imbalanced)
  flip_y = 0.05,          # 5% label noise
  random_state = 123L     # Same seed for reproducibility
)
data_imbalanced <- convert_to_df(py_data_imb)
print("--- Scenario 4: Imbalanced data (from Python) ---")
table(data_imbalanced$Class)


# --- Scenario 5: Imbalanced and asymmetrical data ---
# Using the same parameters as Scenario 4 but with modified V1
py_data_imb_asym <- make_classification(
  n_samples = 1000L,      # 1000 samples
  n_features = 10L,       # 10 total features
  n_informative = 5L,     # 5 predictive features (same as scenario 4)
  n_redundant = 2L,       # 2 redundant features
  shuffle = FALSE,        # first: informative, then: redundant, then noninformative
  n_clusters_per_class = 1L, # Single cluster per class
  class_sep = 1.0,        # Medium separation (same as scenario 4)
  weights = list(0.9, 0.1), # Class ratio 90% to 10% (highly imbalanced)
  flip_y = 0.05,          # 5% label noise
  random_state = 123L     # Same seed for reproducibility
)
data_imbalanced_asym <- convert_to_df(py_data_imb_asym)

# Modify V1 to have asymmetric distributions between classes
modify_v1_asymmetric <- function(df) {
  # Identify classes
  non_events <- df$Class == 0  # non-events (majority class)
  events <- df$Class == 1      # events (minority class)
  
  cat("Non-events (Class 0):", sum(non_events), "samples\n")
  cat("Events (Class 1):", sum(events), "samples\n")
  
  # Modify V1 according to specification
  set.seed(555)  # for reproducibility
  
  # For non-events: N(1, 4) - mean = 1, variance = 4 (sd = 2)
  df$V1[non_events] <- rnorm(sum(non_events), mean = 1, sd = 2)
  
  # For events: N(0, 1) - mean = 0, variance = 1 (sd = 1)
  df$V1[events] <- rnorm(sum(events), mean = 0, sd = 1)
  
  return(df)
}

# Apply V1 modification to imbalanced data
data_imbalanced_asym <- modify_v1_asymmetric(data_imbalanced_asym)

print("--- Scenario 5: Imbalanced and asymmetrical data ---")
table(data_imbalanced_asym$Class)
cat("Variable V1 has been MODIFIED:\n")
cat("- N(1,4) for non-events (Class 0)\n")
cat("- N(0,1) for events (Class 1)\n")


# --- Scenario 6: Real Heart Disease Data ---
# Using the actual heart disease dataset from Usmile package
print("--- Scenario 6: Real Heart Disease Data ---")

# Load the Usmile package and heart disease data
library(Usmile)
data(heart_disease)

# Select only the real clinical variables as specified
real_vars <- c("disease", "age", "sex", "cp", "bp", "chol", "glu", "ecg", "hr", "exang", "stde")

# Create the dataset with only the specified variables
data_real_heart <- heart_disease[, real_vars]

# Remove any rows with missing values
data_real_heart <- na.omit(data_real_heart)

print(paste("Dataset created with", nrow(data_real_heart), "complete cases"))

# Convert cp and ecg to factors with reference level as smallest value
data_real_heart$cp <- factor(data_real_heart$cp, levels = sort(unique(data_real_heart$cp)))
data_real_heart$ecg <- factor(data_real_heart$ecg, levels = sort(unique(data_real_heart$ecg)))

# Convert disease to numeric (0/1) if it's factor
if (is.factor(data_real_heart$disease)) {
  data_real_heart$disease <- as.numeric(data_real_heart$disease) - 1
}

print("Real Heart Disease Data Structure:")
str(data_real_heart)
print("Class distribution:")
table(data_real_heart$disease)
print("Variable summary:")
summary(data_real_heart)

# Save all datasets for future use
save(data_low_power, data_med_power, data_high_power, data_imbalanced, data_imbalanced_asym, data_real_heart,
     file = "classification_datasets.RData")

# Load the datasets to verify
classification_datasets <- load("classification_datasets.RData")

# Save to Excel (make sure writexl package is installed)
if (!require(writexl)) {
  install.packages("writexl")
  library(writexl)
}

write_xlsx(
  list(
    "Low_Power" = data_low_power,
    "Medium_Power" = data_med_power, 
    "High_Power" = data_high_power,
    "Imbalanced" = data_imbalanced,
    "Imbalanced_Asym" = data_imbalanced_asym,
    "Real_Heart_Disease" = data_real_heart
  ),
  path = "classification_datasets.xlsx"
)

cat("\n=== SUMMARY OF ALL SCENARIOS ===\n")
cat("1. Low predictive power: 2 informative features, high noise\n")
cat("2. Medium predictive power: 5 informative features, medium noise\n") 
cat("3. High predictive power: 8 informative features, no noise\n")
cat("4. Imbalanced data: 90/10 class distribution\n")
cat("5. Imbalanced and asymmetrical data: 90/10 class distribution with V1: N(1,4) for non-events, N(0,1) for events\n")
cat("6. Real Heart Disease Data: Actual clinical data with variables: disease, age, sex, cp, bp, chol, glu, ecg, hr, exang, stde\n")

cat("\n=== DATASET CREATION COMPLETE ===\n")
cat("All 6 scenarios have been successfully generated and saved to:\n")
cat("- classification_datasets.RData\n")
cat("- classification_datasets.xlsx\n")
```

## Univariate GLM (logistic regression) models

```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# CODE - U-SMILE WITH CALIBRATION AT THE END AND ROC, PR, U-SMILE PLOTS
# --------------------------------------------------------------------

library(openxlsx)
library(pROC)
library(PRROC)
library(Usmile)
library(ggplot2)

# CONSTANT DEFINITIONS OF INFORMATIVE VARIABLES FOR ALL 6 SCENARIOS
informative_variables <- list(
  low = c("V1", "V2"),           # 2 informative variables
  medium = c("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5"),  # 5 informative variables
  high = c("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6", "V7", "V8"),  # 8 informative variables
  imbalanced = c("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5"),  # 5 informative variables
  imbalanced_asym = c("V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5"),  # 5 informative variables (same as imbalanced)
  real_heart = c("age", "sex", "cp", "bp", "chol", "glu", "ecg", "hr", "exang", "stde")  # all real variables
)

# Helper functions
get_predictor_variables <- function(data) {
  # For synthetic scenarios
  if ("Class" %in% names(data) && any(grepl("^V[0-9]+$", names(data)))) {
    return(paste0("V", 1:10))
  }
  # For real heart disease scenario
  if ("disease" %in% names(data)) {
    predictor_vars <- setdiff(names(data), "disease")
    return(predictor_vars)
  }
  # Default for other scenarios
  return(paste0("V", 1:10))
}

is_variable_informative <- function(variable_name, scenario_name) {
  # Check if variable is informative based on constant definitions
  return(variable_name %in% informative_variables[[scenario_name]])
}

# Function to check data encoding
check_data_encoding <- function(data) {
  cat("=== DATA ENCODING CHECK ===\n")
  
  # Determine target variable name
  target_var <- ifelse("Class" %in% names(data), "Class", "disease")
  
  cat("Target variable:", target_var, "\n")
  cat("Target variable type:", class(data[[target_var]]), "\n")
  cat("Unique values:", unique(data[[target_var]]), "\n")
  
  if (is.factor(data[[target_var]])) {
    cat("Factor levels:", levels(data[[target_var]]), "\n")
  }
  
  class_table <- table(data[[target_var]])
  cat("Class distribution:\n")
  print(class_table)
  
  if (length(unique(data[[target_var]])) != 2) {
    warning("Target variable has more than 2 classes!")
  }
  cat("====================================\n\n")
}

# Cross-validation function WITHOUT CALIBRATION IN ITERATIONS
cross_validate_model_with_calibration_with_usmile <- function(data, formula, n_folds = 10) {
  set.seed(123)
  n <- nrow(data)
  folds <- sample(rep(1:n_folds, length.out = n))
  
  all_predictions_ref <- numeric(n)
  all_predictions_new <- numeric(n)
  all_labels <- numeric(n)
  
  # ADDED: Calculate mean from entire dataset for reference model
  target_var <- ifelse("Class" %in% names(data), "Class", "disease")
  
  # Convert labels to 0/1 for entire dataset
  if (is.factor(data[[target_var]])) {
    overall_labels <- as.numeric(data[[target_var]]) - 1
  } else if (is.character(data[[target_var]])) {
    unique_classes <- unique(data[[target_var]])
    if (length(unique_classes) == 2) {
      class_mapping <- setNames(0:1, sort(unique_classes))
      overall_labels <- class_mapping[data[[target_var]]]
    } else {
      overall_labels <- as.numeric(as.factor(data[[target_var]])) - 1
    }
  } else {
    overall_labels <- as.numeric(data[[target_var]])
  }
  
  # Mean from entire dataset (without fold splitting)
  overall_mean_prob <- mean(overall_labels, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Mean probability (reference model):", overall_mean_prob, "\n")
  
  # ADDED: Store detailed data for each observation
  all_observations <- data.frame(
    fold = integer(n),
    observation_id = integer(n),
    actual_y = numeric(n),
    predicted_prob_ref = numeric(n),
    predicted_prob_new = numeric(n),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (fold in 1:n_folds) {
    train_indices <- which(folds != fold)
    test_indices <- which(folds == fold)
    
    train_data <- data[train_indices, ]
    test_data <- data[test_indices, ]
    
    # Reference model - use mean from entire dataset
    predictions_ref <- rep(overall_mean_prob, length(test_indices))
    
    # Model with variable
    model_new <- glm(formula, data = train_data, family = binomial)
    predictions_new <- predict(model_new, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
    
    all_predictions_ref[test_indices] <- predictions_ref
    all_predictions_new[test_indices] <- predictions_new
    
    # CONVERSION TO 0/1 for test labels
    if (is.factor(test_data[[target_var]])) {
      numeric_labels <- as.numeric(test_data[[target_var]]) - 1
    } else if (is.character(test_data[[target_var]])) {
      unique_classes <- unique(test_data[[target_var]])
      if (length(unique_classes) == 2) {
        class_mapping <- setNames(0:1, sort(unique_classes))
        numeric_labels <- class_mapping[test_data[[target_var]]]
      } else {
        numeric_labels <- as.numeric(as.factor(test_data[[target_var]])) - 1
      }
    } else {
      numeric_labels <- as.numeric(test_data[[target_var]])
    }
    
    all_labels[test_indices] <- numeric_labels
    
    # Save detailed observation data
    all_observations[test_indices, "fold"] <- fold
    all_observations[test_indices, "observation_id"] <- test_indices
    all_observations[test_indices, "actual_y"] <- numeric_labels
    all_observations[test_indices, "predicted_prob_ref"] <- predictions_ref
    all_observations[test_indices, "predicted_prob_new"] <- predictions_new
  }
  
  return(list(
    predictions_ref = all_predictions_ref,
    predictions_new = all_predictions_new, 
    labels = all_labels,
    detailed_predictions = all_observations,
    reference_model_value = overall_mean_prob
  ))
}

# FUNCTION FOR CALIBRATION AT THE END
calibrate_predictions <- function(detailed_predictions) {
  cat("=== PREDICTION CALIBRATION ===\n")
  
  # Prepare data for calibration
  calibration_data <- data.frame(
    actual_y = detailed_predictions$actual_y,
    predicted_prob_new = detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_new
  )
  
  cat("Number of observations for calibration:", nrow(calibration_data), "\n")
  cat("Unique actual_y:", unique(calibration_data$actual_y), "\n")
  cat("Range predicted_prob_new before calibration:", 
      round(range(calibration_data$predicted_prob_new), 4), "\n")
  
  # Calibration model
  calibration_model <- glm(actual_y ~ predicted_prob_new, 
                          data = calibration_data, 
                          family = binomial)
  
  cat("Calibration model coefficients:\n")
  print(summary(calibration_model)$coefficients)
  
  # Calibrated predictions
  predictions_calibrated <- predict(calibration_model, 
                                   newdata = calibration_data, 
                                   type = "response")
  
  # Add calibrated predictions to data
  detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_new_calibrated <- predictions_calibrated
  
  cat("Range predicted_prob_new_calibrated:", 
      round(range(detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_new_calibrated), 4), "\n")
  cat("Mean predicted_prob_new:", round(mean(detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_new), 4), "\n")
  cat("Mean predicted_prob_new_calibrated:", round(mean(detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_new_calibrated), 4), "\n")
  
  return(detailed_predictions)
}

# Metrics calculation function - USES predicted_prob_new_calibrated
calculate_all_metrics_from_detailed_data <- function(detailed_predictions, n_vars_diff = 1) {
  y_actual <- detailed_predictions$actual_y
  y_pred_new_calibrated <- detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_new_calibrated
  y_pred_ref <- detailed_predictions$predicted_prob_ref
  
  results <- list()
  
  # 1. U-smile
  tryCatch({
    raw_data <- data.frame(
      y = y_actual,
      p_ref = y_pred_ref,
      p = y_pred_new_calibrated  
    )
    
    usmile_results <- UScalc_raw(raw_data, y_coef = "rLR", n_vars_diff)
    
    results$usmile <- list(
      netto_Y_nonev = usmile_results$netto_Y_nonev,
      netto_Y_event = usmile_results$netto_Y_event,
      netto_Y_overall = usmile_results$Y_overall,
      p_Y_nonev = usmile_results$p_Y_nonev,
      p_Y_event = usmile_results$p_Y_event,
      p_Y_overall = usmile_results$p_Y_overall,
      # NEW: Add I coefficients
      netto_I_nonev = usmile_results$netto_I_nonev,
      netto_I_event = usmile_results$netto_I_event,
      I_overall = usmile_results$I_overall,
      df = usmile_results$df,
      raw_results = usmile_results
    )
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("UScalc_raw error:", e$message))
    results$usmile <- list(
      netto_Y_nonev = NA, netto_Y_event = NA, netto_Y_overall = NA,
      p_Y_nonev = NA, p_Y_event = NA, p_Y_overall = NA,
      netto_I_nonev = NA, netto_I_event = NA, I_overall = NA,
      df = NA,
      raw_results = NULL
    )
  })
  
  # 2. AUC and AUC-pvalue
  tryCatch({
    if (length(unique(y_actual)) >= 2) {
      roc_obj <- roc(y_actual, y_pred_new_calibrated, quiet = TRUE)  
      results$auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))
      results$auc_pvalue <- calculate_auc_pvalue_v2(y_pred_new_calibrated, y_actual)
    } else {
      results$auc_value <- NA
      results$auc_pvalue <- NA
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("AUC error:", e$message))
    results$auc_value <- NA
    results$auc_pvalue <- NA
  })
  
  # 3. AUC-PR 
  tryCatch({
    if (length(unique(y_actual)) >= 2) {
      pr_curve <- pr.curve(scores.class0 = y_pred_new_calibrated[y_actual == 1],  
                          scores.class1 = y_pred_new_calibrated[y_actual == 0],  
                          curve = TRUE)
      results$auc_pr <- pr_curve$auc.integral
    } else {
      results$auc_pr <- NA
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("AUC-PR error:", e$message))
    results$auc_pr <- NA
  })
  
  # 4. CLLR
  tryCatch({
    results$cllr <- calculate_cllr(y_pred_new_calibrated, y_actual)  
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("CLLR error:", e$message))
    results$cllr <- NA
  })
  
  # 5. Youden metrics
  tryCatch({
    if (length(unique(y_actual)) >= 2) {
      roc_obj <- roc(y_actual, y_pred_new_calibrated, quiet = TRUE)  
      youden_index <- which.max(roc_obj$sensitivities + roc_obj$specificities - 1)
      youden_threshold <- roc_obj$thresholds[youden_index]
      binary_preds <- ifelse(y_pred_new_calibrated >= youden_threshold, 1, 0)  
      
      TP <- sum(binary_preds == 1 & y_actual == 1)
      TN <- sum(binary_preds == 0 & y_actual == 0)
      FP <- sum(binary_preds == 1 & y_actual == 0)
      FN <- sum(binary_preds == 0 & y_actual == 1)
      
      sensitivity <- ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), 0)
      specificity <- ifelse((TN + FP) > 0, TN / (TN + FP), 0)
      precision <- ifelse((TP + FP) > 0, TP / (TP + FP), 0)
      f1_score <- ifelse((precision + sensitivity) > 0, 
                         2 * (precision * sensitivity) / (precision + sensitivity), 0)
      
      results$youden <- list(
        youden_threshold = youden_threshold,
        TP = TP, TN = TN, FP = FP, FN = FN,
        sensitivity = sensitivity, specificity = specificity,
        precision = precision, f1_score = f1_score
      )
    } else {
      results$youden <- list(
        youden_threshold = NA, TP = NA, TN = NA, FP = NA, FN = NA,
        sensitivity = NA, specificity = NA, precision = NA, f1_score = NA
      )
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    results$youden <- list(
      youden_threshold = NA, TP = NA, TN = NA, FP = NA, FN = NA,
      sensitivity = NA, specificity = NA, precision = NA, f1_score = NA
    )
  })
  
  return(results)
}

# FUNCTION FOR CREATING U-SMILE PLOTS 
create_variable_plots_calibrated <- function(detailed_predictions_calibrated, variable_name, scenario_name) {
  plots <- list()
  
  # USE CALIBRATED PREDICTIONS FOR ALL PLOTS
  y_actual <- detailed_predictions_calibrated$actual_y
  y_pred_ref <- detailed_predictions_calibrated$predicted_prob_ref
  y_pred_new_calibrated <- detailed_predictions_calibrated$predicted_prob_new_calibrated
  
  # 1. U-smile plot 
  tryCatch({
    raw_data <- data.frame(
      y = y_actual,
      p_ref = y_pred_ref,
      p = y_pred_new_calibrated  
    )
    
    # Check if sufficient data available
    if (nrow(raw_data) > 10 && length(unique(raw_data$y)) == 2) {
      usmile_results <- UScalc_raw(raw_data, y_coef = "rLR", n_vars_diff = 1)
      
      # Extract netto values for annotations
      netto_nonev <- usmile_results$netto_Y_nonev
      netto_event <- usmile_results$netto_Y_event
      
      # Create custom U-smile plot with modified labels and annotations
      usmile_plot <- USplot(plot_data = usmile_results, y_coef = "rLR")
      
      # Modify the plot with new title, x-axis labels and annotations
      usmile_plot <- usmile_plot +
        ggtitle(paste(scenario_name, "-", variable_name)) +
        scale_x_discrete(
          limits = c('nonev_be', 'nonev_wo', 'event_wo', 'event_be'),
          labels = c("0+", "0-", "1-", "1+")
        ) +
        # Add netto for non-events (top left)
        annotate("text", x = 0.02, y = 0.98, 
                 label = ifelse(!is.na(netto_nonev), paste0("rLR0=", round(netto_nonev, 3)), "rLR0=NA"),
                 hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3, 
                 color = "#0F3C78", fontface = "bold") +
        # Add netto for events (top right)
        annotate("text", x = 4.98, y = 0.98, 
                 label = ifelse(!is.na(netto_event), paste0("rLR1=", round(netto_event, 3)), "rLR1=NA"),
                 hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 3, 
                 color = "#D51424", fontface = "bold") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
          axis.title = element_text(size = 9),
          axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.position = "none"
        )
      
      plots$usmile <- usmile_plot
    } else {
      plots$usmile <- NULL
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error creating U-smile plot:", e$message, "\n")
    plots$usmile <- NULL
  })
  
  # 2. ROC plot
  tryCatch({
    if (length(unique(y_actual)) >= 2 && sum(!is.na(y_pred_new_calibrated)) > 10) {
      # Prepare data in format required by ROCplot
      roc_data_ref <- list(
        y = y_actual,
        p = y_pred_ref
      )
      
      roc_data_new <- list(
        y = y_actual,
        p = y_pred_new_calibrated  
      )
      
      roc_result <- ROCplot(
        data_ref = roc_data_ref,
        data_new = roc_data_new,
        title = paste(scenario_name, "-", variable_name, "(ROC)"),
        alternative = "two.sided"
      )
      
      if (!is.null(roc_result$plot)) {
        roc_plot <- roc_result$plot +
          theme_minimal() +
          theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5))
        
        plots$roc <- roc_plot
      } else {
        plots$roc <- NULL
      }
    } else {
      plots$roc <- NULL
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    plots$roc <- NULL
  })
  
  # 3. Precision-Recall plot 
  tryCatch({
    if (length(unique(y_actual)) >= 2 && sum(!is.na(y_pred_new_calibrated)) > 10) {
      # Prepare data in format required by PRCplot
      pr_data_ref <- list(
        y = y_actual,
        p = y_pred_ref
      )
      
      pr_data_new <- list(
        y = y_actual,
        p = y_pred_new_calibrated  
      )
      
      pr_result <- PRCplot(
        data_ref = pr_data_ref,
        data_new = pr_data_new,
        title = paste(scenario_name, "-", variable_name, "(PR)"),
        n_boot = 100
      )
      
      if (!is.null(pr_result$plot)) {
        pr_plot <- pr_result$plot +
          theme_minimal() +
          theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5))
        
        plots$pr <- pr_plot
      } else {
        plots$pr <- NULL
      }
    } else {
      plots$pr <- NULL
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    plots$pr <- NULL
  })
  
  return(plots)
}

# Function for displaying plots
display_variable_plots <- function(plots, variable_name, scenario_name) {
  cat("\n=== VISUALIZATIONS FOR VARIABLE:", variable_name, "- SCENARIO:", scenario_name, "===\n")
  
  # Check if plots exist for display
  if (is.null(plots) || length(plots) == 0) {
    cat("No plots to display\n")
    return()
  }
  
  # Display each available plot
  plot_names <- names(plots)
  
  for (plot_name in plot_names) {
    if (!is.null(plots[[plot_name]])) {
      cat("--- Displaying plot:", plot_name, "---\n")
      tryCatch({
        print(plots[[plot_name]])
        # Add short pause between plots
        Sys.sleep(1)
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat("Error displaying plot", plot_name, ":", e$message, "\n")
      })
    } else {
      cat("--- Plot", plot_name, "is NULL ---\n")
    }
  }
  
  cat("=== END OF VISUALIZATIONS ===\n\n")
}

calculate_auc_pvalue_v2 <- function(predictions, labels) {
  if (length(unique(labels)) < 2) {
    return(NA)
  }
  if (sum(!is.na(predictions)) < 10) {
    return(NA)
  }
  tryCatch({
    roc_obj <- roc(labels, predictions, quiet = TRUE)
    random_predictions <- rep(0.5, length(predictions))
    random_roc <- roc(labels, random_predictions, quiet = TRUE)
    delong_test <- roc.test(roc_obj, random_roc, method = "delong", alternative = "greater")
    return(delong_test$p.value)
  }, error = function(e) {
    tryCatch({
      roc_obj <- roc(labels, predictions, quiet = TRUE)
      auc_value <- auc(roc_obj)
      n <- length(labels)
      n1 <- sum(labels == 1)
      n0 <- sum(labels == 0)
      Q1 <- auc_value / (2 - auc_value)
      Q2 <- (2 * auc_value^2) / (1 + auc_value)
      se_auc <- sqrt((auc_value * (1 - auc_value) + (n1 - 1) * (Q1 - auc_value^2) + (n0 - 1) * (Q2 - auc_value^2)) / (n1 * n0))
      z <- (auc_value - 0.5) / se_auc
      p_value <- pnorm(z, lower.tail = FALSE)
      return(p_value)
    }, error = function(e2) {
      return(NA)
    })
  })
}

calculate_cllr <- function(scores, labels) {
  true_cases <- as.logical(labels)
  false_cases <- !true_cases
  costs_true <- -log2(scores[true_cases])
  costs_true[is.infinite(costs_true)] <- 1000
  costs_false <- -log2(1 - scores[false_cases])
  costs_false[is.infinite(costs_false)] <- 1000
  n_true <- sum(true_cases)
  n_false <- sum(false_cases)
  cllr <- (sum(costs_true) + sum(costs_false)) / (2 * length(scores))
  return(cllr)
}

# MAIN VARIABLE EVALUATION FUNCTION WITH CALIBRATION AT THE END AND PLOTS ON CALIBRATED DATA
evaluate_single_variable_cv_fixed <- function(data, variable_name, scenario_name, create_plots = FALSE) {
  target_var <- ifelse("Class" %in% names(data), "Class", "disease")
  
  formula_var <- as.formula(paste(target_var, "~", variable_name))
  
  # 1. CROSS-VALIDATION WITHOUT CALIBRATION
  cv_results <- cross_validate_model_with_calibration_with_usmile(data, formula_var)
  detailed_predictions <- cv_results$detailed_predictions
  reference_value <- cv_results$reference_model_value
  
  # 2. CALIBRATION AT THE END ON ALL DATA
  detailed_predictions_calibrated <- calibrate_predictions(detailed_predictions)
  
  # 3. METRICS CALCULATION ON CALIBRATED DATA
  cat("\n=== CALCULATIONS FOR VARIABLE:", variable_name, "===\n")
  metrics <- calculate_all_metrics_from_detailed_data(detailed_predictions_calibrated)
  
  # USE CONSTANT DEFINITIONS OF INFORMATIVE VARIABLES
  is_informative <- is_variable_informative(variable_name, scenario_name)
  
  # 4. PLOT CREATION ON CALIBRATED DATA
  plots <- NULL
  if (create_plots) {
    plots <- create_variable_plots_calibrated(detailed_predictions_calibrated, variable_name, scenario_name)
  }
  
  result_df <- data.frame(
    variable = variable_name,
    usmile_netto_nonev = metrics$usmile$netto_Y_nonev,
    usmile_netto_event = metrics$usmile$netto_Y_event,
    usmile_netto_overall = metrics$usmile$netto_Y_overall,
    usmile_p_nonev = metrics$usmile$p_Y_nonev,
    usmile_p_event = metrics$usmile$p_Y_event,
    usmile_p_overall = metrics$usmile$p_Y_overall,
    usmile_netto_I_nonev = metrics$usmile$netto_I_nonev,
    usmile_netto_I_event = metrics$usmile$netto_I_event,
    usmile_I_overall = metrics$usmile$I_overall,
    usmile_df = metrics$usmile$df,
    auc = metrics$auc_value,
    auc_pvalue = metrics$auc_pvalue,
    auc_pr = metrics$auc_pr,
    cllr = metrics$cllr,
    youden_threshold = metrics$youden$youden_threshold,
    TP = metrics$youden$TP,
    TN = metrics$youden$TN,
    FP = metrics$youden$FP,
    FN = metrics$youden$FN,
    sensitivity = metrics$youden$sensitivity,
    specificity = metrics$youden$specificity,
    precision = metrics$youden$precision,
    f1_score = metrics$youden$f1_score,
    reference_model_prob = reference_value,
    is_informative = is_informative,
    scenario = scenario_name,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  return(list(
    results = result_df, 
    plots = plots,
    detailed_predictions = detailed_predictions_calibrated,  # RETURN CALIBRATED DATA
    cv_data = list(
      y_actual = detailed_predictions_calibrated$actual_y,
      y_predicted_proba = detailed_predictions_calibrated$predicted_prob_new,  # Original predictions
      y_predicted_proba_calibrated = detailed_predictions_calibrated$predicted_prob_new_calibrated, 
      y_predicted_proba_ref = detailed_predictions_calibrated$predicted_prob_ref
    ),
    usmile_raw_results = metrics$usmile$raw_results
  ))
}

# SIMPLIFIED EXPORT TO EXCEL 
export_all_results_to_excel <- function(results_fixed_detailed, filename = "usmile_complete_results.xlsx") {
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  
  # 1. Combined summary sheet for all scenarios
  all_summaries <- list()
  for(scenario_name in names(results_fixed_detailed)) {
    scenario_summary <- results_fixed_detailed[[scenario_name]]$summary
    all_summaries[[scenario_name]] <- scenario_summary
  }
  final_summary <- do.call(rbind, all_summaries)
  
  addWorksheet(wb, "Combined_Summary")
  writeData(wb, "Combined_Summary", final_summary)
  
  # 2. Individual sheets for each scenario with metric results
  for(scenario_name in names(results_fixed_detailed)) {
    addWorksheet(wb, paste0("Results_", scenario_name))
    writeData(wb, paste0("Results_", scenario_name), results_fixed_detailed[[scenario_name]]$summary)
  }
  
  # 3. Sheet with detailed predictions (with predicted_prob_new_calibrated)
  all_detailed_predictions <- list()
  for(scenario_name in names(results_fixed_detailed)) {
    scenario_details <- results_fixed_detailed[[scenario_name]]$detailed
    
    for(var_name in names(scenario_details)) {
      if (!is.null(scenario_details[[var_name]]$detailed_predictions)) {
        pred_data <- scenario_details[[var_name]]$detailed_predictions
        pred_data$variable <- var_name
        pred_data$scenario <- scenario_name
        pred_data$is_informative <- scenario_details[[var_name]]$results$is_informative
        all_detailed_predictions[[paste(scenario_name, var_name, sep = "_")]] <- pred_data
      }
    }
  }
  
  if (length(all_detailed_predictions) > 0) {
    combined_predictions <- do.call(rbind, all_detailed_predictions)
    addWorksheet(wb, "Detailed_Predictions")
    writeData(wb, "Detailed_Predictions", combined_predictions)
  }
  
  saveWorkbook(wb, filename, overwrite = TRUE)
  cat("All data saved to Excel file:", filename, "\n")
  
  return(filename)
}
```
